children: Above-average temperatures are moving out of the U.S. Corn Belt, according to the latest forecast from the NOAA's Climate Prediction Center. The updated 6-10 day forecast shows northern Plains states seeing near-normal temperatures, while above-average temperatures move south. States like North Dakota, South Dakota, and Minnesota are now seeing cooler temperatures, this while receiving more precipitation than normal. However, in its 8-14 day forecast, that heat appears to slowly return to those northern states. CBOT grain futures are up in midday trading, with most-active corn up 0.5%, soybeans up 1.2%, and wheat up 0.5%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
